content: Advance M0120/W0123 with a host-independent 1,000-cycle lifecycle-core qualification. Preserve non-reusable generation, epoch, request replay, and tombstone semantics while making the static authority bounds explicit; do not claim concurrent transport, kernel, QMP, or v1 freeze gates from this stage.

The coordinator retains immutable retirement tombstones and replay records; qualification capacity is enlarged to the calculated 1,000-cycle upper bound rather than introducing eviction or implicit garbage collection. A reset/remove/add cycle consumes two generation candidates, three request records, and two tombstones.

Content revision 72025af adds 4,096 request records, 2,048 tombstones, and a host-independent lifecycle_long_run regression. The fixture passes 1,000 reset/remove/add cycles, checks 2,000 retired generations as DeviceLost, all three mirror callback streams, and replay/conflict behavior.

Focused lifecycle tests passed 4/4 and full development CTest passed 83/83. W0123 remains Active because concurrent memfd/cdev/guest-QMP cycles, kernel sanitizer/fuzz/soak, old-object fault injection, canonical nodes, and lifecycle ABI freeze remain open.
